why: Tried to refute on all four available grounds and none held for the live half. (1) QUOTE: verbatim. llm-gateway-protocol.md line 157 begins exactly 'The request is `GET /v1/models?limit=1000` with a 3-second timeout, and any redirect is treated as failure so the credential can't leak to a redirect target.' The whole line was read: the second sentence ('A gateway that responds slowly or redirects /v1/models, even http to https, fails discovery silently; serve the endpoint directly at the configured base URL') reinforces the conclusion rather than reversing it. (2) CODE: both cited lines say what was claimed. packages/server-core/src/model-fetchers/nestor.ts:41-42 is `await fetch(NESTOR_MODELS_URL, { headers: { 'Nestor-Token': credentials.apiKey ?? '' } })` and packages/shared/src/agent/backend/internal/drivers/anthropic.ts:50 is `await fetch(`${baseUrl}/v1/models?${params}`, { headers })` — no `redirect` option on either, so the WHATWG default 'follow' applies. (3) LAYER UP: nothing mitigates. The only global fetch wrapper is packages/shared/src/config/network-runtime.ts:236-265, which fills in `proxy` and `tls` only and never touches `redirect`; apps/electron/src/main/network-proxy.ts installs an undici dispatcher with no maxRedirections (and fetch-layer redirects are handled above the dispatcher anyway); packages/shared/src/config/network-address-guard.ts is the sibling subsystem (Monitor ws targets and mcp-pool.ts:488), never reached by a model fetch; `Response.redirected` is read nowhere in the repo (grep -a, three hits, all unrelated test doubles named `redirected`). (4) CONSEQUENCE, verified separately from the identifier with a positive control: two local HTTP servers on different ports, the first answering 302 to the second. Node v24.4.1/undici and Bun 1.3.14 behave identically — the redirect target receives `nestor-token` and `x-api-key` while `authorization` and `cookie` are stripped, and `redirect: 'error'` prevents the second request from being made at all. So the credential-forwarding mechanism is real in both runtimes this code runs on. LIVE PATH: the Nestor fetch is the default-on Nessy Gateway provider and runs at startup and on the 60-minute refresh (model-fetchers/index.ts:86-101, registry.ts:26 reuses it for codex-runtime). Checked the escape hatches and they do not apply: inert-worklist §3's nine dated owner decisions (SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD, availableModels/enforceAvailableModels, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath, listSessionSummaries) contain nothing about redirects or model fetches; and this is not a rebrand/subscription product difference — the endpoint shape is Nessy-specific but the no-redirect hardening is orthogonal to branding. The finding survives, but its scope is materially overstated on the Anthropic half and its attacker model is overstated on the Nestor half; see correctedState.
correctedState: CONFIRMED for the Nestor path, OVERSTATED elsewhere. Corrections: (a) 'Both model-list fetches' undercounts and mislabels the population — the repo has four /v1/models-shaped call sites, and only the two cited carry a redirect-surviving credential. agent/diagnostics.ts:162 sends no credential at all (HEAD, unauthenticated reachability probe) and drivers/pi.ts:264 (testOpenAiCompatible) sends `Authorization: Bearer`, which the measured probe shows IS stripped on a cross-origin redirect. (b) The Anthropic half is not reachable in a shipped default build. fetchBackendModels (agent/backend/factory.ts:430) throws CLAUDE_DISABLED_ERROR when provider === 'anthropic' && !isProviderEnabled('claude'), and PROVIDER_FLAG_DEFAULTS.claude is false (feature-flags.ts:129). Even under NESSY_FEATURE_PROVIDER_CLAUDE=1, providerType 'anthropic' is the direct-API path: resolveSetupTestConnectionHint (factory.ts:415) returns 'pi_compat' whenever a baseUrl is present, so anthropic.ts:50 normally targets https://api.anthropic.com and there is no gateway in front of it to emit the 30x. (c) On the Nestor path NESTOR_MODELS_URL is a hardcoded constant (nestor.ts:10, https://code-completion-nestor.tcsbank.ru/api/v1/cli/models), never connection.baseUrl, so the 30x can only come from the corporate gateway itself or from a TLS-terminating proxy the operator already trusted via certStore/tlsCaPath — both of which already hold the JWT in the request they answered. 'A gateway (or a captive proxy in front of one) ... hands the credential to whatever host it names' overstates the attacker model: the exposure the doc actually closes is a trusted-but-compromised or misconfigured gateway forwarding the JWT to a THIRD host, which is real and currently open. Also note the Nestor request matches none of the documented request shape (path is /api/v1/cli/models not /v1/models, no limit=1000, and no timeout at all — the Anthropic-format fetch has a 30s outer budget, the Nestor one has none), because it is Nessy's own corporate-gateway REST endpoint returning a bare NestorModel[] rather than Claude Code's Anthropic-Messages discovery returning {data:[...]}; only the no-redirect hardening transfers. Fix is one line at each site: `redirect: 'error'` on nestor.ts:41 and anthropic.ts:50.
